items.t: MHRA advice for all topical steroids (not a product label): long-term use (generally 6 months or more) of moderate or stronger topical steroids, particularly for eczema, can cause topical steroid withdrawal reactions (intense redness, stinging and burning spreading beyond the treated area). Use the lowest effective potency.

src.q: adverse reactions have been reported following long-term (generally 6 months or more) use of moderate or stronger potency topical steroids, particularly when used for eczema treatment
The lowest potency topical steroid for effective treatment should be used

items.t: BUMPS (topical corticosteroids, diflucortolone named; not a product label): topical corticosteroids can be used in pregnancy. Isoconazole is not covered by this leaflet.

src.q: Topical corticosteroids can be used in pregnancy.

items.t: SPS (all topical corticosteroids; diflucortolone not named individually; not a product label): topical corticosteroids can be used during breastfeeding. Isoconazole is not covered by this page.

src.q: All inhaled and topical corticosteroids can be used during breastfeeding.
